newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Azomures pleased with sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Romania Azomures pleased with sell-off.

text.p: Listed fertiliser maker Azomures SA welcomed the sale of 51 percent of the company to a Romanian trader, saying the move would help it upgrade production, increase its staff and secure gas imports.
"Euro Trading has a five-year investment plan which will help us modernise," Azomures technical manager Vasile Urdea said from the Transylvanian town of Tirgu Mures on Friday.
Euro Trading was the successful bidder for the stake the State Ownership Fund (FPS) sold on Tuesday under a contract pledging the equivalent of $38.7 million in investment.
The FPS announced the sale a day after striking the deal.
Brokers complained that the sell-off of a majority stake in a listed company should be transparent and made known promptly.

The Fund said it had sold to Euro Trading, which already bought stakes in another two Romanian fertiliser makers, 106.8 million Azomures shares at 3,600 lei per share, with 10 percent of the value of the contract already paid for.
Azomures, which joined the bourse a year ago, has stayed at centre-stage ever since mainly due to good financial results. It is the only of 17 stocks to trade on the first tier.

"We find the deal advantageous. Euro Trading gives 10 percent of its stake to Azomures employees," Urdea said, adding that the staff would pay for the 10 percent from dividends. "With payment complete, the stake will be ours."
Azomures currently employs 4,000 people, which Urdea said Euro Trading was planning to increase by 10 percent over the next five years.
Euro Trading officials were not available for comment.
Urdea said Euro Trading had also pledged to secure gas imports for Azomures and grant facilities on fertiliser supplies to Romanian farmers.
Last year, Azomures produced some 1.2 million tonnes of fertilisers, of which 40 percent went to the local market. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
